holidays.name: National Work Like a Dog Day
holidays.description: A day for rolling up your sleeves, tackling your to-do list, and charging at your goals with the tireless energy of a dog chasing a tennis ball. Bonus points for taking a nap afterward.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance listed on the calendar every August 5. It's a nod to the dedication of working dogs, such as herders, guides, and search-and-rescue pups. Its founder is unclear.
holidays.funFact: Dogs have worked alongside people for thousands of years. Herding, hunting, guarding, and guiding are some of their oldest jobs, which makes 'working like a dog' a surprisingly accurate phrase.

holidays.name: National Oyster Day
holidays.description: A day to slurp, shuck, grill, or fry one of the ocean's most famous delicacies. Raw bar fans and Rockefeller lovers can both celebrate.
holidays.origin: The day is tied to Maryland's oyster-harvesting tradition. A Maryland governor reportedly proclaimed August 5 as the day to celebrate the humble bivalve, and it has since become a national food observance.
holidays.funFact: A single oyster can filter up to about 50 gallons of water a day. That makes oysters tiny, tasty water-purifying workers, so they fit in with the day's work theme.
